summary_en.motivation: To develop a crosslinker-free porous bioink with enhanced biocompatibility for cartilage tissue engineering using 3D bioprinting.
summary_en.method: A silk fibroin/decellularized extracellular matrix composite bioink was formulated to create porous scaffolds via 3D bioprinting.
summary_en.result: The printed constructs supported high cell viability and promoted cartilage-specific extracellular matrix deposition.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture and gene expression analysis were performed to assess biocompatibility and chondrogenesis.

papers.title: Adaptive local-global multiscale approach for thermal simulation of the selective laser melting process
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation is a powerful tool for understanding the complex physics of metal additive manufacturing (MAM) processes and to provide guidelines for optimization of the process conditions. The fast kinetics and highly localized nature of the involved phenomena demand high levels of time and space discretization for MAM simulations which significantly increases the computational costs. The existing simplified simulation approaches apply gross approximations to overcome the numerical cost barrier. This study proposes a multiscale approach which breaks down the problem into two scales of local and global simulations. The method argues that a high level of discretization is only required for capturing the physics of fast-kinetics phenomena occurring in the vicinity of the melt-pool, while a much coarser discretization is applicable for the rest of the simulation domain. As a particular type of adaptive submodeling technique, the results of fine-mesh local simulations around the moving melt-pool are combined with the outcome of a coarse-mesh global solution to provide reliable predictions at a significantly reduced computational cost. The efficiency and reliability of the proposed idea has been evaluated for 2D thermal simulation of the selective laser melting process. The outcome of the exercise demonstrates that the methodology can reduce the computational cost of the simulations by an order of magnitude with minimal loss of accuracy.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决金属增材制造热模拟计算成本高的问题。
summary_zh.method: 提出自适应的局部-全局多尺度方法，在熔池附近使用细网格，其余区域使用粗网格。
summary_zh.result: 计算成本降低一个数量级，精度损失极小。
summary_zh.validation: 通过二维SLM热模拟案例验证方法的效率和可靠性。

summary_en.motivation: This study aims to reduce the high computational cost of thermal simulation in metal additive manufacturing by developing an efficient multiscale approach.
summary_en.method: An adaptive local-global multiscale method is proposed, combining fine-mesh local simulations around the melt pool with a coarse-mesh global solution.
summary_en.result: The methodology achieves an order of magnitude reduction in computational cost with minimal loss of accuracy for 2D SLM thermal simulations.
summary_en.validation: The approach is validated on a 2D thermal simulation of the selective laser melting process, demonstrating efficiency and reliability.

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文专注于生物墨水的刚度对干细胞分化的影响，未涉及AI在生物打印中的应用。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate AI/ML into any bioprinting workflow stage; it is purely an experimental biological study without computational or autonomous decision-making components.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究水凝胶生物墨水的刚度对间充质干细胞分化为汗腺的影响。
summary_zh.method: 使用3D生物打印基质培养干细胞并调控墨水刚度。
summary_zh.result: 墨水刚度显著影响干细胞分化为汗腺的效率。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞实验验证分化效果。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how the stiffness of hydrogel-based bioinks influences the differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells into sweat glands within a 3D-bioprinted matrix.
summary_en.method: Mesenchymal stem cells were encapsulated in bioinks of varying stiffness and 3D-bioprinted into matrices, followed by culture and differentiation assays.
summary_en.result: Bioink stiffness significantly modulated the efficiency of sweat gland differentiation, with optimal stiffness promoting differentiation.
summary_en.validation: Differentiation was validated through in vitro immunohistochemistry and gene expression analyses.
